title: Free space from the apt package cache
summary: apt keeps copies of downloaded package files in a cache folder that can grow to gigabytes. You can check its size, clear it, and preview what autoremove would delete. apt downloads the files again if they are needed later.

aliases.text: how much space apt cache takes

prerequisites: Administrator password (sudo) for the cleaning steps

steps.explain: Check how much disk space the apt download cache uses. This is read-only and changes nothing. A large size such as several gigabytes means cleaning will free that much. 'No such file or directory' means the folder does not exist, so there is nothing to clean.
steps.expect: One line with a size and the path, e.g. '8.0K    /var/cache/apt/archives' on a fresh system or '1.2G    /var/cache/apt/archives' when the cache is full.

steps.explain: Delete all downloaded package files (.deb) from the apt cache. Installed programs are not affected. apt downloads a package again if you install it later.
steps.expect: Usually no output. A line 'WARNING: apt does not have a stable CLI interface' may appear first; it is harmless.

steps.explain: Preview which packages apt would remove as unused. --dry-run only prints the plan; nothing is removed. A summary ending in '0 to remove' means there is nothing to clean up. This card does not remove packages; review the list before doing any real removal.
steps.expect: Lines 'Reading package lists...' and a summary such as '0 upgraded, 0 newly installed, 0 to remove and 4 not upgraded.'

verify.expect: A small size, e.g. '12K    /var/cache/apt/archives', after the cache was cleaned.

source.title: apt manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
